Summary: Make the startup measurement measure what it names
Description: Re-scoped after escalation; the floor statistic this story previously carried is withdrawn. cold_start_first_text_ms has never measured a cold start: scripts/measure-startup.mjs launches the packaged app 8 times two seconds apart, sorts, and takes the median, so only launch 1 is ever cold and the reported figure is warm by construction on macOS, while on ubuntu-latest seven of eight launches never print MARK first_text and are silently dropped, making the median an n=1 over an unidentified launch. Gating on the minimum of a round is therefore inverted: the minimum is the warmest launch, so the gate would defend a number no reader experiences and would get easier as the runner cache improved. This story fixes the measurement and nothing else: diagnose and fix the Ubuntu drop-out, record launches in launch order, and split the metric into cold_start_first_text_ms (launch 1 and only launch 1) and warm_start_first_text_ms (the median of launches 2..N), then point the existing CI rule at the warm metric under its true name with every number unchanged. fixtures/perf-budgets.json is deliberately not in the paths. Deriving the CI numbers is MARXY-70; restoring enforcement of the 500 ms product budget is MARXY-69. Reasoning, rejected alternatives and the ADR-0022 amendment text: docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-18-cold-start-metric-falsified.md. Evidence: the escalation object in orchestration/results/MARXY-19.json. Do not change any product budget, do not remove or soften any check, do not let CI write to the repository, and do not make anything advisory.
Acceptance: 1. The Ubuntu drop-out is diagnosed and fixed, not gated around: the PR body names the mechanism by which seven of eight launches failed to print MARK first_text, with evidence from a CI job on this branch (captured stderr, exit codes and per-launch timing, not speculation), and links a green ubuntu-latest job on this branch whose results/perf.json records usable_runs equal to runs_n. The usable_runs assertion in criterion 5 is in the same diff as the fix and not before it. 2. scripts/measure-startup.mjs never sorts the raw sample. results/perf.json carries runs in launch order and a launches array with one entry per attempted launch carrying index, ms (null when no mark), ok, exit_code and stderr_tail, including the launches that produced no mark. 3. The record separates the two quantities by name and carries cold_start_first_text_ms (the elapsed time of launch 1 and only launch 1), warm_start_first_text_ms (the median of launches 2..N), warm_runs, warm_runs_n, runs_n, usable_runs, cold_warm_ratio (cold divided by the warm median; recorded and printed, not yet gated), cold_procedure (a non-empty string naming what made launch 1 cold; "process-cold only" is a legitimate value), env_class and runner_class. The key cold_start_first_text_ms never holds a statistic computed over more than launch 1. 4. node scripts/measure-startup.mjs --selftest exits 1 for each of the following as separately named cases: a record missing any key listed in criterion 3; warm_start_first_text_ms not equal to the median of a fixed synthetic launch-order list with launch 1 excluded; launch 1 included in the warm statistic; cold_start_first_text_ms not equal to element 0 of that list; a runs array written in sorted order when the synthetic input was unsorted; usable_runs less than runs_n. 5. pnpm gate:perf exits 1, in both modes, when results/perf.json has usable_runs below runs_n, when cold_start_first_text_ms is absent, when cold_procedure is absent or empty, or when warm_runs_n is below 8. Each is a separately named gate-perf --selftest case, because a floor over one sample is not a floor and a cold number that is silently missing is worse than one that is wrong. 6. The rule that gates in CI is unchanged in every number and changed only in which key it reads: warm_start_first_text_ms is compared against min(product.cold_start_first_text_ms * multiplier, baseline_ms * 1.10) using the values already in fixtures/perf-budgets.json, the CI failure message names the quantity as a warm start, and a check in the PR asserts fixtures/perf-budgets.json is byte-identical to its state on main. 7. Reference mode gets stricter and never weaker: it exits 1 when warm_start_first_text_ms exceeds 500, and additionally exits 1 with a message stating that the ADR-0013 product cold-start budget is not currently enforceable and naming MARXY-69 as the story that restores it. Both are selftest cases. 8. Nothing becomes advisory: a check in the PR asserts that .github/workflows/ci.yml contains no continue-on-error and no || true on the measurement, selftest or gate:perf steps, and that all of them remain required on both runner classes. 9. No case is lost and the withdrawn mechanism leaves no residue: every selftest case name from the MARXY-55 suite still exists, adapted only where a key was renamed; the combined gate-perf --selftest and measure-startup --selftest case count is asserted to be at least 24; and rg -n "floor_ms|floor statistic|minimum of the" over scripts/ returns nothing. 10. docs/adr/0022-perf-budgets-two-tier-enforcement.md carries Amendment 1, "the metric split", exactly as drafted in docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-18-cold-start-metric-falsified.md: it withdraws the floor-statistic amendment that never landed, replaces the two wrong sentences named there, states that CI does not measure a scaled version of the reader experience, and writes any clause whose numbers this story does not measure as an obligation naming the story that discharges it. docs/adr/README.md shows ADR-0022 amended and CHANGELOG.md has a line under Unreleased.

Summary: Read CR-only documents as carefully as LF ones
Description: A markdown file with classic-Mac line endings parses to a tree whose code-block ranges are wrong: contentRange, infoString and openingFenceLineEnd search for a bare newline, so a fenced block content collapses to an empty range past its own text and its info swallows the rest of the block. Rewriting the 527 conformance inputt line endings gives LF 0 violations, CRLF 0, CR-only 198 CODE_CONTENT violations across 182 parses. Nothing consumes those ranges yet because apps/desktop still renders with markdown-it (MARXY-61); an operation would splice at the wrong offset the moment one does (ADR-0004). Found by the MARXY-11 round-2 review, which also found that the isJustTheCode NUL substitution has no check.
Acceptance: 1. conformance.test.ts runs every rule case and every generated case through all three line-ending rewrites (LF as written, LF to CRLF, LF to CR) and asserts zero AST_INVARIANTS violations for each with GFM on and off; the check fails before the fix with roughly 198 CODE_CONTENT violations and passes after. 2. A named test asserts that for a CR-only fenced block with an info string the codeBlock content slices to the code lines alone, lang is the language and info is the language rather than the rest of the block, and that a CR-only indented block content slices to its code lines alone. 3. A NUL-in-code case exists for both a fenced and an indented block, and reverting the isJustTheCode NUL substitution fails it. 4. No indexOf or split on a bare newline literal remains anywhere in packages/core/src/parse outside a comment, asserted by a test over the source text, so the next line-ending assumption cannot be added silently. 5. pnpm gate:golden output is byte-identical, since no corpus fixture uses a lone CR and the goldens must not move.

Summary: Prove CommonMark conformance in CI without vendoring the spec
Description: MARXY-11 first acceptance criterion is that the CommonMark spec suite passes on HTML equivalence, but the spec examples are CC-BY-SA-4.0 and the orchestrator ruled they do not ship, so what always runs is 527 inputs of ours against the BSD-2-Clause oracle and ci.yml never calls test:spec. That is strong but it is not the spec suite. The licence rule forbids vendoring the examples, not fetching them in CI, where no product code runs and the no-network rule does not apply. Found by the MARXY-11 round-2 review.
Acceptance: 1. A CI step fetches spec.json for a version pinned in exactly one place in the repository to a path outside the working tree and runs the spec check, failing the build on any HTML divergence or any AST invariant violation, proved by a run that shows the example count. 2. The script verifies the fetched file SHA-256 against a digest committed in the repository and refuses a mismatch, proved by a test that feeds it a file with the wrong digest and asserts exit 1; a digest is a fact rather than the content, so committing it does not vendor the examples. 3. A test asserts the fetch path resolves outside the repository root, and git status --porcelain is empty after the step, asserted in the workflow itself. 4. The step is required rather than advisory: a check asserts ci.yml carries no continue-on-error and no || true on it. 5. ADR-0021 records that the examples are checked and never vendored, naming the pinned version and digest, and docs/adr/README.md stays accurate.

Description:
ADR-0013's 500 ms cold-start budget is currently enforced nowhere, and has not been since before MARXY-55. The reference tier reads the same cold_start_first_text_ms written by the same eight-launch median; MARXY_PERF_ENV=reference changes which ceiling the number is compared against but not what the number is, so docs/sdlc.md's release runbook step 2 compares a warm median against a cold budget and fails in the lenient direction: the warm number is the smaller one, so the gate passes while the product budget is being missed by roughly 5x. This story makes the reference tier measure a genuine cold start and rewrites the runbook step to say which quantity it enforces. Depends on MARXY-63, which creates the cold launch as a separate recorded quantity. Reasoning: docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-18-cold-start-metric-falsified.md, decision 2. Do not change any product budget number and do not make anything advisory.

Sequenced behind MARXY-71 as well as MARXY-63: the statistic this story enforces is read from MARK first_text, and MARXY-71 is what makes that mark mean paint rather than a frame count. With the honest numbers now on record (2844 ms on macOS, 1735 ms on Linux) criterion 3 lands a reference-mode gate that is red by design until the author rules on the cold-start budget. That is deliberate and it is not a reason to delay this story: what it blocks is MARXY-16, not itself. The ruling is recorded in orchestration/needs-human.md and this story must not pre-empt it by changing the product number.
Acceptance: 1. In MARXY_PERF_ENV=reference a round is k cold launches with k at least 5 (default 5), each preceded by the cold-making step and separated by enough idle for it to take effect, and no warm launch enters the reference statistic. results/perf.json records cold_launches (in launch order), cold_launches_n and cold_procedure naming the step actually performed. 2. The cold-making step is executed by the script where it can be and is never implied where it cannot: it kills any running marxy process, purges the OS file cache only where a password-less mechanism exists on that platform, and otherwise records cold_procedure as "process-cold only" rather than claiming more. docs/sdlc.md documents the same step as a runbook step a human can follow. 3. Reference mode compares median(cold_launches) against product.cold_start_first_text_ms with no multiplier and no tolerance: a 501 ms cold median exits 1 and a 500 ms cold median exits 0, each a named gate-perf --selftest case. 4. Reference mode exits 1, each as a separately named selftest case, when cold_launches_n is below 5, when cold_procedure is absent or empty, when env_class is not reference, when results/perf.json is missing, and when any launch not certified cold appears inside the cold statistic. 5. The placeholder failure MARXY-63 added to reference mode ('the product cold-start budget is not currently enforceable') is removed and replaced by the real comparison in the same diff; a selftest case asserts reference mode now fails on a 501 ms cold median rather than on the placeholder, and rg -n 'not currently enforceable' over scripts/ returns nothing. 6. docs/sdlc.md release runbook step 2 states which quantity it enforces, names MARXY_PERF_ENV=reference and the results/perf.json artifact path, requires cold_launches_n of at least 5 and a recorded cold_procedure in the artifact attached to the tag, and says plainly that a tag cut without it has not measured what the reader feels. 7. Every number in the product object of fixtures/perf-budgets.json is byte-identical to its value on main, asserted by a check in the PR that reads both revisions; that file is not in this story paths. 8. Nothing becomes advisory: a check in the PR asserts .github/workflows/ci.yml still contains no continue-on-error and no || true on the measurement, selftest or gate:perf steps. 9. No case is lost: every selftest case name present after MARXY-63 still exists, and the combined case count is asserted to be at least 30. 10. ADR-0022 Amendment 2 records the reference-tier procedure and statistic, replacing the sentence named in docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-18-cold-start-metric-falsified.md; docs/adr/README.md and CHANGELOG.md updated.

Summary: Derive the CI perf numbers from cross-run evidence, waive or adopt each baseline, gate the cold ceiling
Description:
Every CI number in fixtures/perf-budgets.json was derived from a quantity that has since been falsified: macos-latest baseline 1901 ms is a warm median and ubuntu-latest baseline 7719 ms is a median over one unidentified launch from a broken sample. This story re-derives them from the corrected metrics MARXY-63 produces, adds the absolute cold ceiling the cold metric needs, and adds confirmation-by-re-measure. The decisive constraint is that the variance is between runs, not within them: macOS warm clusters sit at ~380-560, ~1470-1760 and ~1800-2060 ms across three jobs, a 4x movement of the whole distribution, while inside any one job the cluster spans only 1.15-1.5x, so a spread guard computed over one round sees tightness and wrongly concludes the class deserves a baseline. macos-latest is expected to take the baseline_waived path; the escape is measurement, not a wider tolerance. Depends on MARXY-63 and on MARXY-69 (both edit scripts/gate-perf.mjs). Reasoning: docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-18-cold-start-metric-falsified.md, decisions 1 and 4. Do not change any product budget number, do not make anything advisory, and do not let CI write to the repository.

Inherits the MARXY-71 ordering through MARXY-69, for the same reason and more sharply: this story writes adopted baselines and cold envelopes into fixtures/perf-budgets.json, and numbers adopted against a mark that is about to move would have to be re-derived the moment it moves.
Acceptance: 1. Evidence before numbers: the PR body links at least five CI jobs per runner class, at five distinct commits on main or on this branch, each recording cold_start_first_text_ms, warm_start_first_text_ms and usable_runs equal to runs_n. fixtures/perf-budgets.json records them under ci.<class>.observed_cold_ms and ci.<class>.observed_warm_ms, each observation carrying commit, job_id and runner_image. 2. The spread guard is cross-run and never within-round: spread equals max(observed_warm_ms) divided by min(observed_warm_ms) over those observations, and node scripts/gate-perf.mjs --selftest exits 1, each as a separately named case, for fewer than five observations, for observations that do not carry distinct commits and job ids, for a tolerance below 1.05, and for spread times tolerance above 1.20. A further named case asserts that a configuration whose within-round dispersion is tight but whose cross-run spread is 4x is rejected, because that is the configuration macos-latest presents. 3. macos-latest records baseline_ms null together with a baseline_waived block carrying reason, observed_warm_ms, cross_run_spread, escalated_to and date, and keeps the envelope and the cold ceiling, unless its measured cross-run spread satisfies criterion 2 at a tolerance of at least 1.05, in which case the block is absent and the PR body shows the numbers that justified the baseline. baseline_ms null without baseline_waived exits 1, and a baseline_waived missing any required key exits 1, each a named selftest case. 4. ubuntu-latest re-derives baseline_ms from the corrected warm measurements; the 7719 ms value is not carried forward. For every class that keeps a baseline, baseline_ms equals max(observed_warm_ms), asserted by a named selftest case. 5. The CI tier gains an absolute cold ceiling: cold_start_first_text_ms is compared against ci.<class>.cold_envelope_ms, derived as ceil(max(observed_cold_ms) * 1.3), with no baseline and no tolerance applied to the cold metric. Its derived_from records commit, runner_image, the observations, and the statement that the previous multiplier was derived from a warm median and is therefore superseded. Selftest: under the ceiling exits 0, above it exits 1, a missing cold_envelope_ms exits 1. 6. Confirmation before failure, in ci mode only, applies to both metrics: a breach re-measures through an injected measurement function for up to two further rounds and fails only when every round breaches. Named selftest cases prove that three breaching rounds exit 1 with output naming all three rounds and their margins; that a breach followed by a clean round exits 0, prints a line containing the words confirmed noise with the first round margin, and records every round in the result record; that a clean first round exits 0 having called the measurement function zero extra times, asserted by a call counter; and that reference mode never re-measures. 7. cold_warm_ratio below 1.0 exits 1 in ci mode with a message that a first launch faster than the warm median was not cold and the measurement is invalid. The PR body shows the observed minimum ratio across the criterion 1 observations, justifying the threshold; a named selftest case covers it. 8. runs_n is part of every baseline and cold-envelope record and the gate exits 1 when results.runs_n differs from the runs_n recorded for that runner class, proved by a named selftest case, so a statistic is never compared against a number taken at another sample size. 9. Every number in the product object of fixtures/perf-budgets.json is byte-identical to its value on main, asserted by a check in the PR that reads both revisions; a check asserts .github/workflows/ci.yml has no continue-on-error and no || true on the measurement, selftest or gate:perf steps; both runner classes still gate both metrics. 10. ADR-0022 Amendment 3 records the adopted tolerance, baselines, cold envelopes and any waiver per runner class, superseding the adoption values in the original ADR; docs/adr/README.md and CHANGELOG.md updated; the combined selftest case count is asserted to be at least 40.

Summary: Rest first_text on a paint signal rather than a frame count
Description:
MARXY-13 made the paint wait observable by counting animation frames, which is a real improvement over asserting by ordering, but frames are not paint. With #doc set to visibility hidden the smoke check still reports 21 blocks, 919 chars and frames ticking while the window shows nothing, because the evidence function reads textContent. So the number the ADR-0013 cold-start budget is measured against can be produced by a build that renders nothing a reader can see. Found by the MARXY-13 round-2 review. Sequenced behind MARXY-63, which fixes the harness that consumes the mark.

Moved to phase 0 and sequenced ahead of MARXY-69 and MARXY-70. Those two adopt cold ceilings, baselines and the 500 ms reference comparison against MARK first_text, and this story says that mark can be emitted by a build that renders nothing a reader can see. Adopting numbers taken against a mark that is known to be about to move is the same error the whole cold-start thread exists to correct: the name of the measurement doing the thinking instead of the measurement.
Acceptance: 1. MARK first_text is emitted only after a signal the engine gives for rendering, a PerformanceObserver paint or first-contentful-paint entry or an equivalent verified to exist in both WebKit and WebKitGTK, and MARK painted records which signal it used. 2. A negative test in the same PR: with #doc set to visibility hidden the CLI smoke check exits non-zero, where today it passes with frames ticking. 3. A negative test: with requestAnimationFrame replaced by a setTimeout shim the check exits non-zero. 4. MARK first_text keeps its exact two-field form and scripts/measure-startup.mjs needs no change to parse it, asserted by a test. 5. The frames >= 2 assertion from MARXY-13 survives unchanged, so this adds a requirement rather than replacing one.

Summary: Let pnpm build succeed on a machine that cannot paint
Description: apps/desktop/package.json hardcodes MARXY_SMOKE_REQUIRED=1 on the build script, so pnpm build takes 62 seconds and then fails on any machine whose display is asleep, where the webview receives no animation frames. pnpm build is in the definition of done (AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md), and the fleet runs overnight on a laptop that sleeps, so as it stands every story will eventually report a red build for a reason that has nothing to do with its diff. The danger is not the red itself but the fix a future agent reaches for, which is deleting the frames assertion MARXY-13 spent two attempts landing. The strictness must survive: CI must still fail when a build that can paint does not paint. Found by the MARXY-13 round-3 review, which reproduced it.
Acceptance: 1. On a machine that delivers no animation frames, pnpm build exits 0 within the time it takes to build, prints the skip reason naming the environment, and prints the sentence telling the reader that the frame assertion is not what is wrong; proved by a repro recorded in the PR body (display asleep or over ssh with the screen locked). 2. In CI both runner classes still require the smoke check: a check asserts the workflow sets MARXY_SMOKE_REQUIRED=1 (or the equivalent) for the build step on both classes, and that neither continue-on-error nor || true appears on it. 3. A build that can paint and does not paint still fails: with afterPaint neutralised on a machine that delivers frames, pnpm build exits non-zero, asserted by a named test. 4. The required mode is still reachable by hand: MARXY_SMOKE_REQUIRED=1 pnpm build exits non-zero in the frameless state, asserted by a test. 5. docs/sdlc.md states which of the four definition-of-done commands may skip on which grounds and which may never skip, so the next agent does not have to infer it.

Summary: Put the missing attack vectors in the hostile fixture
Description: MARXY-12 sanitises 27 vector families but fixtures/corpus/10-hostile.md carries only a few of them, so the acceptance criterion that the hostile fixture yields no dangerous output is satisfied largely by probe strings inside the test file rather than by the corpus the gates sweep. Missing from the fixture: srcdoc, formaction, srcset, poster, MathML, base, template, namespaced elements such as svg:script, and entity sequences that are only dangerous after a second decoding pass. Fixture bytes are frozen, so extending one is its own story with its own golden update. The point is that every gate which sweeps the corpus, including gate:no-network in both engines and any future screenshot gate, then exercises these vectors for free rather than only the unit suite doing so.
Acceptance: 1. fixtures/corpus/10-hostile.md gains a section per missing family, each labelled with what it is, covering at least srcdoc, formaction, srcset, poster, MathML, base, template, a namespaced element and a double-encoded javascript scheme. 2. Every pre-existing byte of the file is unchanged, asserted by a check in the PR that the previous content is a prefix of the new file, so no existing golden or expectation shifts for a reason unrelated to the addition. 3. pnpm gate:golden goldens are regenerated in the same PR and the diff shows only additions. 4. A test asserts the sanitiser removes every newly added vector, and neutralising the sanitiser fails at least one test per added family. 5. pnpm gate:no-network stays green over the corpus in both engines with zero remote requests, and its unsanitised control still observes requests from the new sections, proving the additions are reachable by the gate rather than inert text. 6. The two exploits found by the MARXY-12 review are in the fixture as their own sections and are the regression test for them: a backslash-authority image reference of the form src=''/\host/pixel.png'', and a self-closing anchor whose dropped end tag swallows the rest of the document. Both would have been caught by gate:no-network in the corpus sweep rather than by a reviewer, which is the argument for this story.

Summary: Catch the normalisations the fidelity gate still lets through
Description:
MARXY-14 made gate:fidelity compile and drive the shipped save path, and the reviewer then mutated that path to find what the gate still lets through. Recomposing an NFD sequence to NFC inside write_atomic survives the entire gate, because every corpus fixture is already NFC - and on macOS decomposed content arrives from the filesystem routinely, so this is a normalisation a reader would actually meet. Trimming trailing whitespace is caught only by one unpinned byte in 09-gfm-everything.md, so a tidy-up of that fixture would silently delete the coverage. A lone-CR normalisation escapes the corpus half entirely and is caught only by the Rust unit tests, which the mutants never run through - so the two halves of the gate cover different things and only one half is mutation-verified. None of these is a defect in the save path today; each is a guard missing against the day someone helpfully normalises.

Moved to phase 0 with MARXY-77 and kept strictly after it. Splitting the two across a phase boundary would leave two stories editing scripts/gate-fidelity.mjs weeks apart on branches that go stale against each other, and this story's case names are written against the path MARXY-77 creates. Not split: every criterion is a mutation case in one file.
Acceptance: 1. A fixture or gate-owned payload carries NFD sequences, and a mutant that recomposes NFD to NFC inside the shipped save path turns gate:fidelity red, named individually in the output. 2. A mutant that trims trailing whitespace is caught by a byte the gate pins: the corpus precondition check names the fixture and the trailing whitespace it requires, so removing that whitespace fails the gate instead of removing coverage. 3. A mutant that normalises a lone CR to LF is caught by the corpus half of the gate, not only by the Rust unit tests. 4. The mutants run through the Rust unit tests as well as the round trip, asserted by a mutant that only those tests can catch turning the gate red. 5. Every payload in 1-4 is reported by name whether it passes or fails, and a check asserts the gate has no skip path that can hide one. 6. The shipped save path is unchanged by this story: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/atomic_write.rs is byte-identical to its state on main at the end of the PR, asserted by a check that reads both revisions, because a mutant that lives in the diff is not a mutant but a defect. The gate harness applies every mutant to a copy of the source and a named case proves the copy, not the tracked file, is what was mutated.

Summary: Make the review order a computed thing rather than a habit
Description: Review, not implementation, is the constraint. Nine stories sit In Review against eight merges; six of their pull requests are BEHIND main and three are in conflict. cycle.mjs updates every BEHIND branch on every cycle, so one merge re-runs CI across the whole queue - and because approvals are now signed against the commit they were read at (orchestration/approve.mjs), that same update voids every signed approval in the queue. The validity window of an approval therefore shrinks as the queue grows, which means the queue cannot be drained by reading faster: it has to be shortened and ordered. This story makes the order a computed, printable thing; the loop is taught to act on it by the story that follows. The order is phase first, from orchestration/deps.json, lowest phase number first, because the plan is sequenced to de-risk in phase order. Then disturbance, descending: the number of other open pull requests whose changed files intersect this one's, so the branch that will invalidate the most approvals lands before those approvals are signed rather than after. Then age, oldest first, as the tiebreak so nothing starves. A conflicted pull request is not in the order at all. ADR-0025 records the decision and is proposed until this story lands it. Read docs/sdlc.md and orchestration/README.md before starting; do not change any merge condition cycle.mjs already checks.
Acceptance: 1. node orchestration/review-order.mjs prints JSON with an order array of {key, pr, phase, disturbs, ageHours, behind, dirty} for every story whose state is in_review and which has a PR number, and an excluded array whose entries each carry a why string. 2. The sort is phase ascending, then disturbs descending, then ageHours descending (oldest first), then key, and a separately named selftest case proves each of the four keys decides the order in turn while the ones before it tie. 3. disturbs for a pull request is the number of other pull requests in order or excluded whose changed-file set intersects its own; the always-shared files CHANGELOG.md, docs/taste-review/queue.md, pnpm-lock.yaml and orchestration/results/*.json are excluded from the intersection, because every pull request touches them and a metric that scores every PR alike says nothing; named cases prove a PR sharing no file scores 0, one sharing a file with three others scores 3, and two PRs sharing only CHANGELOG.md both score 0. 4. A pull request whose mergeStateStatus is DIRTY or whose mergeable is CONFLICTING appears only in excluded, with why naming the conflict, never in order; a named case covers it. 5. A story that deps.json places in more than one phase, or in none, makes the script exit 1 naming the story and the phases, because an order that cannot say which phase a story is in cannot order it; a named case for each of the two failures. 6. node orchestration/review-order.mjs --selftest runs every case against fixture boards committed under orchestration/test/, exits 1 if any case fails, and prints a case count of at least 12. 7. GitHub is read through exactly one injectable function so the selftest can replace it; a named case asserts the selftest calls the real one zero times and makes no network request. 8. docs/sdlc.md gains a section 'Review order and the review WIP limit' stating the three sort keys in order and why disturbance is descending; that a conflicted PR is returned rather than queued; that a returned story does not count against the review WIP, because a return moves the story out of In Review and a return is the same unit of work rather than a new one; and that a returned story re-enters the order at its own phase, disturbance and original age rather than at the head, so it cannot starve by being returned. 9. docs/adr/0025-review-order-and-review-wip.md moves from proposed to accepted in this PR, docs/adr/README.md lists it, and CHANGELOG.md has a line.

No hold reason is lost: a named case asserts the list of hold-reason strings cycle.mjs can print is a superset of the list it could print before this PR, with the before-list committed as a fixture. 8. orchestration/README.md documents reviewLanes, the one-update-per-cycle rule and the approve-time checks; CHANGELOG.md has a line.

Summary: Gate the repository settings so branch protection cannot drift back
Description: MARXY-6's criteria are GitHub repository settings, so nothing in the tree notices when one of them is changed or was never set. Measured on 2026-09-18, one of them was never set: enforce_admins is false, so a direct push to main by the admin account the fleet uses is not rejected, and no open pull request has ever reported REVIEW_REQUIRED even though PR #11 edits packages/core/src/sanitize/ and PR #10 amends an accepted ADR, both CODEOWNERS paths. This story adds the standing check that would have said so. It reads the settings through gh api in an explicit live mode and never in CI, because reading branch protection needs admin and no gate may depend on a secret; what runs in CI is the selftest over committed fixtures, which is what stops the check itself rotting. This story does not change any setting - that is MARXY-6, and it is the author's. Restart 2026-09-19: the live required check is the single context ci (MARXY-6 / hygiene applied 2026-09-18). Summary: Prove the sanitiser never makes the live tree deeper than intended
Description: The sanitiser rebuilds markup from policy without a full HTML tree builder, which is right, and the property that makes it right was established by measurement during review: of 35 tree shapes, 22 diverge from what a real parser builds, every divergence is shallower than intended, and the only ancestor anything ever gains is an implied table, tbody or tr. Depth is what matters, because an element that gains an ancestor can be captured by it - which is how a formatting element swallows the rest of a document. Today that property holds by argument and by one reviewer run. It should hold by a harness, because the next change to the writer is where it would quietly stop being true.
Acceptance: 1. A harness compares the sanitiser output tree against both engines for a case list covering at least the 35 shapes measured in review, and fails if any node gains an ancestor other than an implied table section. 2. The harness fails when the writer is mutated to close an element late, demonstrated by a named mutation in the output. 3. The case list is asserted by value, so adding or removing a shape is a decision recorded in the diff. 4. The harness runs in the gate on both engines, with no skip path that can become the silent default, asserted by a check.

Description: MARXY-197 sat blocked for hours: planner-trigger.mjs held all dispatch on 'planner due', nothing ever ran state.mjs planned to clear it once the planner's PR (MARXY-189, a docs/plan/deltas/ landing) merged, and that same landing plus its board-sync siblings (MARXY-188, MARXY-186, MARXY-178) padded the ops-window count and merge-count that made the planner due in the first place, near-guaranteeing the next cycle re-triggers on its own output. Prior deltas (docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-20-after-165.md) already hit this and could only tell a human to run the command by hand.
Acceptance: 1. When cycle.mjs lands a PR whose merged diff adds a file under docs/plan/deltas/, it runs the equivalent of `state.mjs planned` itself in that same cycle (stamping lastPlan and mergesAtLastPlan) instead of relying on a human to run it after the fact - covered by a cycle fixture asserting lastPlan/mergesAtLastPlan are set after landing such a PR with no manual step. 2. A merge that landed a plan delta (recorded via that stamp) is excluded from the ops-window count in plannerReasons, so a run of planner-landing PRs cannot make the ops-majority reason fire on itself - planner-trigger.test.mjs case. 3. In cycle.mjs, the merge-count, weekly-age and ops-majority planner reasons become advisory only: ready stories still dispatch while the planner is due for those reasons alone. Dispatch is still held when the planner has never run ('never planned') or when an unread escalated/blocked story is the reason. A cycle fixture covers both: cadence-only due still dispatches ready stories; never-planned or fresh escalation still holds them. 4. When the planner is due and cursor-agent is on PATH (and not --dry-run), cycle.mjs starts the planner headlessly the same way it starts implementors via dispatch.mjs, instead of only printing that it is due; when cursor-agent is absent it still just names the planner as due, as today. 5. docs/sdlc.md and orchestration/README.md describe the corrected cadence: what still holds dispatch, what only advises, and that a landed plan delta self-records instead of needing a manual state.mjs planned. 6.
